name: Avery Lai
life: “I still remember practicing a greeting in a dark shopfront.” On Friday, near the steps at Pier Beach, Avery watches the working part of the waterfront before turning toward the open water.
voice: I used it to practice asking for my old job back. A customer heard and offered me a different one.
appearance: Avery has a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Look for short copper curls. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a mustard canvas overshirt with a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it. In conversation Avery holds eye contact until the other person has finished.
personality: Avery feels a room through sound. A door slammed in high spirits can produce the same instant startle as an angry one, and it takes a little while to hear what actually follows.
agenda: To interview for the unexpected job.
family: Caroline Diaz is Avery’s aunt by marriage. Avery asks before bringing somebody along. Caroline can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The returned daughter*, Caroline says, “I raised her after she left. I want her to know going back doesn't cancel the years she calls me Mum.”
connections: Marisol Lane. A new interview and an old wedding both turn up unexpectedly in reflections.

reactions.situation: A client asks to sit outside the shared mirror's view
reactions.response: Avery puts the person's chair outside the reflection and lets them choose when to look.
